subject: Cognitive Science
title: The Availability Heuristic
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Availability Heuristic usable.

hook.text: After a plane crash makes headlines, ticket sales drop—even though flying just got statistically no less safe.

buildup.text: We judge frequency by how easily examples come to mind. Vivid events feel common; quiet ones feel rare.

discovery.text: Tversky and Kahneman named this the availability heuristic: ease of recall replaces actual probability.

twist.text: Shark attacks feel more likely than falling coconuts. Reality: coconuts kill more people every year.

climax.text: Media amplifies this bias. Whatever is covered most feels most dangerous, regardless of real data.

punchline.text: If you can picture it, you overestimate it.

quiz.question: What does the availability heuristic use to judge frequency?
